conclusion: Complete first-layer brim ownership and adaptive interface finishing remain valid. Endpoint-only chaining can miss short strokes beside the interior of a long path even when the material footprint is connected. Project onto the receiver and use a short local detour through the unchanged fragment instead of retracing a connector. Keep rounded beads in the planned support island and away from brim/other roles; preserve height, flow ratio, non-reversible direction and global receiver closure. Require no printable-width lost footing. The reviewed test2 Release retains all three old short strokes inside continuous runs, with zero independent submillimetre Support or Support interface extrusions. Model/higher support geometry, six Brim paths and 0.17 mm contacts remain unchanged. Repeated exports have identical instructions. This is source-bound software evidence, not a universal physical-print guarantee.
scope: Reviewed native first-layer interior splicing, regressions and deterministic test2 Release exports as of 2026-10-25.
